en: Great-uncle Walter had been the family's cheerful {{spendthrift}} for forty years, buying yachts he never sailed.
At eighty-one he was still {{irrepressible}}, arriving at every dinner with some fresh scheme.
Relatives had tried for years to {{admonish}} him sternly about money, but the warnings never seemed to land.
Each {{admonition}} grew more severe, until the family lawyer finally sent one in writing.
Year after year, his habits had {{erode|eroded}} what remained of the family fortune.
He stayed as {{lavish}} in private as in public, filling his sister's hallway with flowers nobody asked for, simply because giving pleased him.
About his spending he stayed flatly {{obstinate}}, refusing to change a single habit.
The one person he still listened to was a new partner named Feld, whose damp handshake relatives found {{repulsive}}.
When the family finally confronted the pair, the meeting turned {{acrimonious}} within minutes.
Only his {{tenacious}} niece refused to leave until he signed papers cutting Feld off from the accounts.
zh: 四十年来，沃尔特舅公一直是家里那位乐呵呵的败家子，买过好几艘从没出过海的游艇。
都八十一岁了，他还是那股压不住的劲头，每次家庭聚餐都揣着个新点子登场。
亲戚们这些年没少板着脸训诫他花钱大手大脚，可警告好像总没说进他耳朵里。
一次比一次严厉的告诫下来，最后干脆变成了家庭律师寄来的一封正式信函。
年复一年，他的这些习惯把家族剩下的那点财产一点点蚕食殆尽。
他私底下和人前一样出手阔绰，把妹妹家的走廊摆满了没人要的鲜花，纯粹是送礼这件事本身让他高兴。
一提到花钱的事，他就是铁了心地固执，一个习惯都不肯改。
他唯一还听得进去话的人，是一位叫费尔德的新搭档——亲戚们都觉得此人那双湿冷的手让人反胃。
等家人终于把这两人叫来对质，会面没几分钟就吵得剑拔弩张。
只有他那位锲而不舍的侄女不肯离场，非要他签字把费尔德从账户里彻底踢出去才罢休。

passages.title: 山间修道院的新人
en: Mei arrived at the mountain convent already {{credulous}}, believing every ghost story the older novices told her.
The nuns lived a famously {{chaste}} life, having sworn off marriage and romance decades earlier.
Duties rotated daily, and the chores were so {{interchangeable}} that no one minded who swept which hall.
New arrivals were expected to stay {{docile}}, doing exactly as told without ever asking why.
Villagers below the mountain would {{extol}} the abbess's patience and her quick hands at mending nets.
When Mei broke curfew once, an old nun pleaded on her behalf, and that {{intercession}} spared her from expulsion.
Months of shared meals and chores gave Mei something she had never had: a sense of {{belonging}}.
Her training would {{culminate}} each spring in a quiet ceremony before the whole community.
Not everyone welcomed that ceremony; the elders' debate over its old rites turned {{acrimonious}} this year.
Only one {{tenacious}} old nun refused to let a newer, shorter version replace it.
zh: 小梅刚到山上修道院的时候就轻信得很，老修女们讲的鬼故事她句句都当真。
这里的修女过着出了名的清修生活，几十年前就发誓不再谈婚论嫁。
杂务每天轮换，各项活计彼此可以随意替换，谁扫哪间厅堂都无所谓。
新来的人都得温顺听话，让做什么就做什么，从不多问一句为什么。
山下的村民常常夸赞院长的耐心，还有她补渔网那双利落的手。
有一回小梅犯了宵禁，一位老修女替她向院长求情，正是这次说情才让她免于被逐出山门。
几个月一起吃饭、一起干活，小梅头一次有了一种归属感。
她的修习每年春天都会以一场面向全体修女的静默仪式画上句点。
并不是所有人都欢迎这场仪式；今年长老们为旧规矩该不该保留吵得很不客气。
只有一位锲而不舍的老修女不肯让一套更新、更短的版本取而代之。

passages.title: 运输站的零件荒
en: The dispatch office sat right beside the highway {{interchange}}, where three trucking routes met before the bridge.
A sudden {{scarcity}} of replacement brake parts had grounded half the fleet by Tuesday morning.
Nobody at the depot could {{account-for|account for}} why the last shipment had vanished from the manifest.
The dispatcher, usually calm, grew {{irritable}} by midday, snapping at anyone who asked the same question twice.
Drivers waiting in the yard tried to {{repress}} their frustration, pacing instead of shouting.
One veteran driver just sat {{expressionless}} through the whole ordeal, giving away nothing on his face.
Beyond the parts problem lay a deeper {{dearth}} of veteran mechanics willing to work nights, a gap no parts order could fix.
The frustration reached its {{culmination}} when three drivers refused to move their rigs, blocking the yard entirely.
Talks between the union and management turned {{acrimonious}} that same afternoon.
The shop steward alone stayed {{tenacious}} enough to keep both sides talking past dinner.
zh: 调度室就设在高速公路立交桥旁边，三条货运线路在过桥前正好在这里交汇。
刹车配件突然告急，到周二早上已经有一半车队被迫趴窝。
站里没人说得清楚，最后一批货怎么会从提货单上凭空消失。
平时沉得住气的调度员，到了中午也变得毛毛躁躁，谁把同一个问题问两遍都要挨他一顿呛。
等在场院里的司机们强压着火气，只是来回踱步，没人真嚷嚷起来。
有位老司机全程面无表情地坐着，脸上什么情绪都没露出来。
配件短缺背后，其实是更深一层的问题：愿意上夜班的资深修理工严重匮乏——这个缺口，任凭订多少配件都补不上。
怨气最终在三名司机拒绝挪车时达到顶点，场院被彻底堵死。
就在当天下午，工会和管理层的谈判变得剑拔弩张。
全靠那位工会代表一人锲而不舍，硬是让双方谈到了晚饭时间之后还没散。

passages.title: 老饕的晚宴传奇
en: Every year, the aging epicure grew {{sedulous}} about the dinner critics still discussed decades later.
His voice was famously {{mellifluous}}; guests swore they would listen to him read a grocery list.
He was a master of {{apophasis}}, vowing never to mention his rival's disastrous souffle, then describing it for ten minutes.
New guests mistook his elaborate manners for pure {{affectation}}, though old friends knew it was how he had always been.
Decades of critics sneering at his early cooking had {{indurate|indurated}} him against every insult that followed.
One uninvited food blogger had the sheer {{effrontery}} to correct his seasoning at the table.
His assistant, a man of relentless {{officiousness}}, kept refilling glasses nobody had asked him to touch.
Only a pinch of saffron, {{infinitesimal}} in size, went into each dish, yet the flavor filled the room.
When a rival chef arrived uninvited, their exchange turned {{acrimonious}} within seconds.
Still, the old host stayed {{tenacious}} about his recipes, changing not one measurement in forty years.
zh: 这位年迈的美食家每年都为那场几十年后评论家们仍津津乐道的晚宴，操心得格外勤勉。
他的嗓音出了名的甜润动听，宾客们都说就算他念购物清单也愿意听下去。
他最擅长欲言又止的把戏，嘴上信誓旦旦说绝口不提对手那盘失败的舒芙蕾，接着却花了十分钟把它描述了个遍。
初次见面的客人常把他那套繁复的礼数当成矫揉造作，可老朋友都清楚，他向来就是这个样子。
几十年来评论家对他早年手艺的冷嘲热讽，早把他磨炼得对后来的一切侮辱都无动于衷。
有个不请自来的美食博主竟厚颜无耻到当着满桌人的面，指点他调味的对错。
他的助手是个好管闲事到没边的人，不停给客人斟酒，压根没人请他动手。
每道菜里放的藏红花不过极小极小的一撮，香味却弥漫了满屋子。
一位对手厨师不请自来，两人几句话没说完，场面就变得剑拔弩张。
尽管如此，老主人对自己的食谱依旧锲而不舍地坚持，四十年来一个分量都没改过。

passages.title: 镇文书与老桥之争
en: For thirty years, Mrs. Alvarez served as the {{conduit}} between the town council and residents too shy to attend meetings.
She would {{sympathize}} with whoever knocked on her door, no matter how small the complaint seemed.
The job itself was surprisingly {{strenuous}}, full of long hours chasing paperwork through three departments.
Her final year proved unusually {{eventful}}, dominated by a fight over the old stone bridge.
The bridge's biggest {{proponent}} was a retired engineer who had crossed it every morning for forty years.
He argued its closure would be a merely {{transient}} inconvenience compared with losing town history.
Younger members disagreed, and the argument turned {{acrimonious}} at the very first meeting.
Mrs. Alvarez stayed {{tenacious}} throughout, refusing to let either side leave before finding common ground.
To everyone's surprise, the two sides parted {{agreeably}} in the end, shaking hands over a compromise plan.
In the end, it was pure {{caprice}} — a coin toss — that decided which contractor got the job.
zh: 三十年来，阿尔瓦雷斯太太一直是镇议会和那些不好意思去开会的居民之间的沟通桥梁。
不管谁敲开她的门，抱怨的事听着多鸡毛蒜皮，她都愿意听、愿意体谅。
这份工作其实出乎意料地费力，常常要花大把时间在三个部门之间追着文件跑。
她任内最后一年格外多事，几乎都被那场围绕老石桥的争执占满了。
这座桥最坚定的支持者，是一位退休工程师，他每天早上走过这座桥已经走了四十年。
他辩称，比起失去一段镇史，封桥带来的不便不过是转瞬即逝的小事。
年轻些的议员们不认同，第一次开会争论就变得剑拔弩张。
阿尔瓦雷斯太太始终锲而不舍，不找到双方都能接受的办法，谁也别想离场。
出乎所有人意料，双方最后握手言和，愉快地就一套折中方案达成了共识。
到头来，决定这单工程花落谁家的，竟是一次纯属心血来潮的抛硬币。

passages.title: 遗嘱背后的伪造
en: When the village founder died, his family met to divide his modest estate.
His nephew wanted to {{deify}} him with a statue and offerings, like a saint.
Several cousins felt {{aggrieved}}: the nephew had promised them land long ago and never delivered.
The family lawyer's manner was {{shifty}}, though no one could prove he'd done wrong.
Two cousins were caught in a huddle that was unmistakably {{conspiratorial}}, plotting to force him to open his files.
The polite reading of the will soon {{degenerate|degenerated}} into a shouting match.
By week two the family had turned {{disputatious}}, arguing over furniture, though no one threatened to sue.
The lawyer had used a neat {{artifice}}: forging the notary's initials, then swapping a signed page.
When the forgery surfaced, the argument turned {{acrimonious}} — sharp words in icy, clipped tones.
The one cousin who refused to drop it stayed {{tenacious}}, spending months on old bank records, and finally forced a confession from him that was utterly {{ignominious}}.
zh: 村里的创始人过世后，家人聚到一起，商量怎么分他留下的那点薄产。
侄子一心想把他奉为神明，立了尊雕像，逢年过节还要供上祭品，把他当成圣人供着。
好几个堂表兄弟都憋着一肚子委屈——侄子当年答应分给他们地，这么多年过去了却始终没兑现。
家族律师说话做事总有点鬼鬼祟祟，可谁也拿不出他做了什么亏心事的证据。
深夜里，两个堂兄弟被撞见凑在一起交头接耳，密谋着要逼他交出档案。
本来只是心平气和地宣读遗嘱，没过多久就吵成一团。
到了第二周，全家人已经吵得不可开交，为家具争来争去，倒也没谁真闹到要打官司。
原来律师耍了个巧妙的手段：他模仿公证员的签名，趁机把签好的那页偷偷换掉了。
伪造的事一曝光，争执立刻变得剑拔弩张，双方话说得又冷又硬。
唯独一个堂兄弟不肯善罢甘休，翻查了几个月的旧银行记录，最终逼出了他一句颜面扫地的认罪。

passages.title: 编辑部风波
en: Mei's first month was mostly {{mundane}}: formatting copy, fetching coffee, though never short of gossip.
Her editor's one real {{exhortation}} — a rule, not a plea — was simple: verify every name and number twice.
The newsroom felt {{cosmopolitan}} — correspondents swapping stories in five languages over lunch.
One {{careless}} slip — a swapped digit in a casualty count — made it into print.
A colleague passed over for the job grew visibly {{envious}}, wishing it and its byline were hers.
The error {{diminish|diminished}} her editor's trust, and for a week she was kept on desk duty.
Rather than sulk, Mei stayed {{receptive}}, asking her editor to mark up her next draft in red.
Her next assignment sent her to a crossing that was {{perilous}}, used by smugglers and soldiers alike.
She checked every figure with a thoroughness that was {{tenacious}}, leaving the fact-checkers nothing to fix.
When the colleague accused her of favoritism, the exchange turned {{acrimonious}} — sharp words, but nothing louder than a hiss.
zh: 美怡在编辑部的第一个月过得平平淡淡：不是排版就是端咖啡，倒是办公室的八卦从没断过。
主编唯一一条正经的告诫不是恳求，而是一条铁律：姓名和数字，一律核对两遍。
编辑部气氛倒是格外国际化——记者们午饭时能用五种语言你一言我一语地聊开。
美怡头一篇稿子出了个粗心的差错——伤亡人数里一个数字敲错了，愣是被印了出去。
一个没被选上这个任务的同事看着明显眼红，直说这活儿、连带那份署名，本该是她的。
这次失误让主编对她的信任打了折扣，接下来一周她只能待在桌前打杂。
美怡没闹脾气，反倒虚心受教，主动请主编把她下一篇稿子改得满纸红字。
她接到的下一个任务是前往一处边境通道，那里十分凶险，走私客和士兵常年出没同一条路。
她铆足了劲把每个数字都核对了一遍，锲而不舍到核实人员都挑不出错。
那位同事在会上当众指她走后门，两人当场唇枪舌剑，话虽尖利，却谁也没提高嗓门。

passages.title: 河堤修缮令
en: After generations of flooding blamed on the river's {{meandering}} course — looping back on itself — the governor vowed to straighten it.
She issued a formal {{decree}}: every landowner must reinforce their section of the levee by spring.
The {{promulgation}} of the order caught residents by surprise.
Officials responsible for one stretch had been openly {{negligent}}, letting the stones crumble untouched for years.
Reports of {{sporadic}} leaks along that stretch had been filed for months, each one quietly forgotten.
Then the water rose to a genuinely {{unprecedented}} height.
The stagnant floodwater left a smell of rot and diesel that was {{revolting}}, hanging across the lower streets for weeks.
Rebuilding the levee was brutally {{monotonous}} work — one sandbag after another, for a month straight.
Only the young engineer stayed {{tenacious}}, tearing up failed drafts night after night until she found a workable design.
At the town hall meeting, the argument with the officials who'd let it crumble turned openly {{acrimonious}} — voices sharp, never raised.
zh: 这条河弯弯绕绕，自己给自己打起结来，几代人以来的水患都算在它头上，新上任的州长发誓要把它取直。
她颁布了一道正式法令：沿岸所有地主必须在开春前把各自负责的河堤段加固好。
法令来得太快，公布出来时居民们都没反应过来。
负责其中一段河堤的官员一直敷衍塞责，任由石堤多年失修、坍塌都没人管。
那段河堤时不时渗水的报告递交了好几个月，每一次都被悄悄搁在一边、不了了之。
后来一场春汛，水位涨到了前所未有的高度。
积水久久不退，腐臭混着柴油味，弥漫在低洼街区数周不散，闻着让人反胃。
重修河堤是件枯燥透顶的苦差——一袋接一袋地扛沙包，一干就是整整一个月。
唯有那位年轻的工程师锲而不舍，一份份撕掉失败的图纸，熬到深夜也要重画，直到设计出一套真正撑得住的方案。
镇民大会上，她跟那些放任河堤坍塌的官员吵了起来，言辞激烈，却始终没人提高嗓门。

passages.title: 塔楼守护人称号
en: For time {{immemorial}} the Voss family had kept the title Keeper of the Tower, older than the charter.
Such posts were {{sinecure|sinecures}}: a stipend for showing up on festival days, and nothing else.
Old Voss enjoyed a local {{eminence}}, greeted with a bow in the market square.
He was also famously {{loquacious}}, turning a greeting into a twenty-minute story about the tower's founding.
A visiting historian proved {{hypercritical}}, picking apart the founding story for inconsistencies.
She found the treasury still {{denominate|denominated}} his stipend in a currency unminted for two centuries.
She found the charter never named the Voss family — a clerk had invented the claim.
Warned twice to drop it, the young solicitor stayed {{tenacious}} and found the discrepancy after three weekends in the archive.
At the hearing, a routine correction turned {{acrimonious}} — sharp-tongued, but never raised to a shout.
He signed a formal {{abjuration}}, though the tower itself — {{impregnable}} for six centuries — had never once needed defending.
zh: 沃斯家族世代把持着“守塔人”这个礼仪头衔，据说比镇上的建镇宪章还要古老，年代已不可考。
这类差事向来都是闲差：守塔人只需在节庆日露个面，就能领一份津贴，别的什么也不用做。
老沃斯在镇上颇有几分声望，走过集市时人人都要向他欠身致意。
他还出了名地能说会道，一句寒暄都能扯出二十分钟关于塔楼来历的故事。
一位来访的历史学家却出了名地爱挑刺，把这段家族史的每个细节都翻出来找破绽。
她发现镇库账上，他的津贴至今仍以一种停止铸造了两百年的旧币计价。
她还发现，宪章原文里压根没提过沃斯家的名字——那不过是某个抄写员当年编出来的说法。
这位年轻的律师被自家事务所劝退了两次，却始终不肯放手，在档案室泡了三个周末，终于揪出了破绽。
听证会上，本该是一次寻常的更正，却吵得言辞尖刻，好在谁也没提高嗓门喊起来。
老人最终正式签字放弃了这个头衔，可那座塔楼本身——六百年来固若金汤——却从没真被攻打过一次。

passages.title: 拆穿伪造案
en: Detective Okafor had earned some {{renown}} for closing cases other units had abandoned.
Her newest target, a forger, had evaded capture so long her captain doubted she'd ever {{apprehend}} him.
When her last case collapsed, two colleagues stopped by just to {{commiserate}}, bringing coffee and saying little.
She was known to be {{ruthless}} in interrogation, pressing suspects without any way to save face.
Her captain insisted on the {{primacy}} of physical evidence over any hunch.
The forger's paperwork was flawless, and the team stayed {{puzzled}}, with no thread to pull.
Okafor stayed {{tenacious}} through the captain's repeated orders to close the file, rereading the same documents every night.
The detail she caught was {{subtle}}: the forger had misspelled his own company's name consistently.
When she brought it to the captain, the meeting turned {{acrimonious}} — his voice clipped, hers colder still.
Only once the forger confessed did the rest {{buttress}} her theory, and the captain never quite apologized.
zh: 奥卡福警探专啃别的警队都啃不动的案子，也因此小有名气。
她这回盯上的一个造假犯，多年来一直逍遥法外，连她自己的队长都怀疑她这辈子都抓不到人。
上一起案子在法庭上翻了车后，两个同事跑来她桌前，只是想表示一下慰问，带了杯咖啡，也没说出什么中用的话。
她在审讯室里出了名地不留情面，能把嫌疑人盘问上几个钟头，连个台阶都不给对方留。
她的队长却坚持认为，物证的分量始终该压过任何直觉。
那个造假犯的文件做得天衣无缝，整个小组愣是困惑了好一阵子，愣是找不到一丝线索。
面对队长三番五次让她结案的命令，奥卡福依旧不肯罢休，每晚都把同一批文件翻出来重读。
让她终于抓到把柄的，是一个不起眼的细节：造假犯每次都把自己那家假公司的名字拼错成同一个样子。
她把这个破绽拿给队长看时，两人当场就吵了起来——队长的语气生硬，她的更是冷冷的。
直到造假犯认了罪，队里其他人才拿出证据佐证她的判断，队长却始终没正儿八经地道过歉。

passages.title: 老锁匠
en: Frank had run his shop from the same storefront for thirty years, and a new chain never made him less {{tenacious}}.
Everyone at the shop knew forcing a stuck lock too fast could {{impair}} a wrist for good.
That happened to one apprentice, and the local paper's {{condemnation}} followed all spring.
When a customer defended him at a town meeting, his {{uncontainable}} gratitude sent him outside.
He'd always been {{argumentative}} with adjusters, though he never once raised his voice.
Across town, his former apprentice Dale ran a rival chain, and the two stayed {{antipathetic}} for reasons neither could name.
Frank found Dale's habit of quoting fake competitor rates plainly {{contemptible}}.
A reporter covering the closing turned out unexpectedly {{sympathetic}}, letting him talk an hour before mentioning the lawsuit.
What actually {{intrigue|intrigued}} her, she admitted, was a drawer of hand-cut keys untouched for years.
She noticed, too, the {{prominent}} callus on his thumb, worn by decades of a hand file.
zh: 弗兰克在同一个门面里开了三十年锁匠铺，街对面新开的连锁店抢再多生意，也没让他少一分执着坚持。
店里人都清楚，锁卡得太死还硬撬，很容易把手腕彻底弄坏。
他手下一个学徒就是这么倒的霉，那年春天，本地报纸对锁匠铺的口诛笔伐没完没了。
一次镇民大会上，一位老主顾替他说了话，他那股按捺不住的感激当场把自己逼出了会场。
他跟保险理算员总是争个不停，可从没在理赔办公室外头跟人红过脸。
城那头，他从前的学徒戴尔开了家新连锁店，两人多年来互相看不顺眼，具体为什么，谁也说不清。
戴尔惯用编造的对手报价去压低价格，弗兰克觉得这种做法实在卑劣。
派来报道店铺关门的记者出乎意料地富有同理心，任他讲了整整一个钟头往事，直到最后才提起官司的事。
她事后坦言，真正勾起她兴趣的，其实不是那桩丑闻，而是抽屉里那些多年没人碰过的手工钥匙。
她还注意到他拇指上那道显眼的老茧，那是他几十年握着锉刀留下的印记。

passages.title: 湿地保卫战
en: Lena's {{lifelong}} devotion to the wetlands began the summer a developer tried to drain them.
Her {{advocacy}} eventually got the marsh declared protected, though it took nine years of hearings.
Councilman Voss led the {{opposition}} to nearly everything she proposed after that.
Word was, his {{grudge}} over a zoning vote she'd blocked years earlier had never faded.
Some said he'd spent months quietly {{machinate|machinating}} to get her voted off the board.
Their meetings grew so {{acrimonious}} that the clerk began timing speakers with a stopwatch.
Yet Lena stayed {{tenacious}}, showing up to every hearing for a decade regardless of the empty room.
What she found truly {{loathsome}} was that his own firm had quietly dumped runoff into the marsh.
A young board member turned out surprisingly {{empathetic}}, and cast the deciding vote after hearing her describe the herons vanishing.
Even Voss later admitted he'd come to {{advocate}} for the wetlands himself, once tourists started paying to see them.
zh: 莉娜对那片湿地的守护始于开发商想把它填平建停车场的那个夏天，从此便是一辈子的事。
她四处奔走呼吁，湿地终于被列为保护区，但这场拉锯经历了整整九年的听证会。
从那以后，沃斯议员几乎逢她提案必反对，理由好像纯粹是看她不顺眼。
据说他还在为多年前一次被她搅黄的区划投票耿耿于怀。
有人说他私底下花了好几个月，暗中盘算怎么把她挤出规划委员会。
两人在台上的交锋越来越针锋相对、字字带刺，镇文书干脆掏出秒表给发言人计时。
可莉娜就是不肯松劲，哪怕会场常常空无几人，十年间场场听证会都没落下过。
真正让她齿冷的是，他自己的建筑公司多年来一直在悄悄把未经处理的废水排进那片湿地。
委员会里一位年轻成员出乎意料地感同身受，听她讲到白鹭一年年消失后，投下了关键一票。
多年后，沃斯私下也承认，如今连他自己都开始为湿地说话了，毕竟游客现在肯掏钱来看这片地方。

passages.title: 老裁缝的谢幕
en: I joined the atelier at the single most {{inopportune}} moment possible, the week Auguste first mentioned retiring.
Our {{renowned}} tailor, Auguste, was nearing seventy but still had a three-year waitlist for one suit.
His {{debonair}} manner made him easy to love — a silk square and a half-bow for every client.
Our morning {{banter}}, coffee in hand, was an atelier tradition, ten minutes of insults before the first pin was threaded.
That season, a younger designer, Theo, began meeting a magazine editor to {{conspire}} against him.
Their plan, it seemed, was to slowly {{undermine}} Auguste's reputation before fashion week.
The magazine ran an outright {{slander}}, claiming he'd stolen patterns from his own apprentices for years.
Backstage before the show turned {{acrimonious}}, Auguste and Theo trading insults by the racks.
One of his oldest clients sent a written {{entreaty}}, begging him not to walk away.
He stayed {{tenacious}} through it all, and closed the show himself, needle and thread in hand.
zh: 我加入工坊的时机糟糕到不能再糟——正是奥古斯特头一回提起想退休的那一周。
我们那位声名远播的老裁缝奥古斯特，眼看就要七十岁了，一件西装的预约还要排上三年。
他风度翩翩，一方丝巾别在胸前，见谁都要微微欠身，让人没法不喜欢他。
早晨喝咖啡时的插科打诨早成了工坊的老传统，第一根针落下前总要先斗嘴十分钟。
那一季，一位年轻设计师泰奥开始私下频繁约见一位杂志编辑，暗中勾结起来对付他。
据大家猜测，他们的算盘是趁时装周之前慢慢搞垮奥古斯特的名声。
那家杂志干脆造谣中伤，说他这些年一直在偷学徒们的版型。
后台在开场前变得剑拔弩张，奥古斯特和泰奥当着衣架的面互相人身攻击。
他一位相熟多年的老主顾给他写了一封恳求信，求他千万别就这么离开这个品牌。
他始终咬牙坚持了下来，亲自为这场秀收尾，手里还捏着针线。

passages.title: 暗房旧事
en: The negatives sat in a box for sixty years, and {{oxidization}} ate silvery holes through several.
Someone had once {{superimpose|superimposed}} a second exposure over the original, doubling a dancer's arms into a blur.
Silverfish got into the box too, and years of quiet {{depredation}} left the edges lace-thin.
The dancer in the best print was impossibly {{voluptuous}}, scandalizing the photographer's own studio.
My intern, a sharp but {{impertinent}} kid, kept asking why I hadn't scanned it all sooner.
Our {{repartee}} over the light table was the one part of the job I looked forward to.
The collector after them was an old woman who stayed {{tenacious}}, calling weekly for a year and refusing any answer but yes.
When an argument between her lawyer and my director over price turned {{acrimonious}}, I kept scanning.
Reporters kept asking whether the dancer was really who she claimed, and I stayed {{impassive}} throughout.
My director finally had to {{exhort}} me to speak before the story ran without us.
zh: 底片在潮湿的盒子里放了整整六十年，氧化早把好几张底片蛀出了银灰色的破洞。
曾经有人把第二次曝光叠印在了原片上，把一个舞者的手臂叠成了一团模糊的残影。
盒子里也进过衣鱼，经年累月的蚕食把底片边缘啃得薄如蝉翼。
那张最好的照片正中，那位舞者丰满性感得过分，据说当年没少让摄影师自己的工作室脸红。
我那个实习生脑子挺灵，就是嘴上没大没小，老问我干嘛不早点把整箱底片扫描完。
在读片台前跟他斗嘴调侃，倒成了这份工作里我最盼着的一段时光。
一直惦记这些照片的那位藏家，是个执拗到底的老太太，一年来每周都打电话，非要个“行”字不可。
她的律师跟我们主任为了价钱吵得不可开交，我在一边只管接着扫描。
记者们不停追问照片里的舞者是不是藏家说的那个人，每次采访我都是一副波澜不惊的样子。
主任最后实在忍不住，催我随便说点什么，免得报道出来时我们一句话都没有。

passages.title: 被抹去的发明人
en: Ada had spent thirty years working in near-total {{obscurity}}, in a rented lab behind a hardware store.
Pryce built his fortune on her formula and never missed a chance for {{ostentation}}, gold cufflinks included.
When she first brought her notebooks to the patent board, its {{closed-minded}} chairman waved them away unread.
He {{dismissively}} told her the formula obviously belonged to whoever had the money to manufacture it.
Rebuilding her case felt {{daunting}}, but she spent the next two years doing exactly that.
The {{litigation}} that followed dragged on for nearly a decade.
Reporters covering the trial said she seemed to {{exemplify}} every inventor history had erased.
Courtroom exchanges between the two lawyers grew increasingly {{acrimonious}}, especially once the old notebooks were read aloud.
Her role in the product, once celebrated, had been {{diminished}} to a single footnote.
She stayed {{tenacious}} to the end, and the settlement finally put her name back on the patent.
zh: 艾达在五金店后面租的那间实验室里默默无闻地干了将近三十年。
普莱斯正相反，靠她的配方发了家，从不放过任何一个招摇的机会，金袖扣都不例外。
她第一次把笔记本送到专利局时，那位思想僵化的主席看都没看就把它们推了回去。
他轻蔑地告诉她，这配方显然该归谁有钱谁生产。
从头再来打这场官司让人望而生畏，可她还是花了整整两年硬着头皮去做。
随之而来的诉讼拖了将近十年。
报道庭审的记者说，她仿佛就是历史悄悄抹去的每一个发明人的缩影。
双方律师在法庭上的交锋越来越剑拔弩张，尤其是那些旧笔记本被当庭念出来之后。
她在那项产品里的贡献，曾经也算风光一时，如今早被压缩成了一条不起眼的脚注。
她硬是咬牙坚持到了最后，和解协议终于把她的名字重新写回了专利上。

passages.title: 花园保卫战
en: Mrs. Okafor had always been the garden committee's most {{amiable}} member, warm to newcomers who shared nothing else with her.
The developer's plan to pave the plots into parking left her quietly {{resentful}} for weeks.
At the town hall, three residents rose to deliver a scathing {{denunciation}} of the scheme.
One called it {{deplorable}} that the board would trade a garden for parking.
The newest member, a retired judge, was famously {{litigious}} and had an injunction drafted that same night.
Not everyone dug in: the compost-bin couple stayed {{amenable}}, open to any plan that spared the fruit trees.
The developer's own representative sat through two hours of questions without answering one, looking entirely {{unresponsive}}.
Only the town planner offered anything {{nuanced}}, weighing the parking shortage against a decade of harvests.
It took the committee's {{tenacious}} chair four months of setbacks before the developer backed down and the road was rerouted.
Only that redrawn map finally {{assuage|assuaged}} the residents' anger.
zh: 在花园委员会里，奥卡福太太一向是最和蔼可亲的一个，见了新来的人，哪怕跟自己毫无交集，也照样笑脸相迎。
开发商一提出要把这片共用菜地铺成停车场，她也一连好几个星期闷闷不乐、心怀怨恨。
在镇民大会上，三位居民先后起身，对这项方案作了措辞严厉的公开谴责。
有人当场就说，董事会拿一座花园换几个停车位，简直是可耻之举。
委员会最新加入的成员是位退休法官，一向好打官司，当晚散会前就已经在拟禁制令了。
也不是人人都寸步不让：管堆肥箱的那对夫妻倒挺好说话，只要方案能保住那几棵果树，怎么改都行。
开发商派来的代表倒是坐了整整两小时，一个问题都没答上来，全程爱理不理。
唯独镇里的规划师拿出的方案称得上考虑周全，把停车位紧张和十年收成放在一起权衡，没有一味偏袒哪一方。
委员会那位锲而不舍的主席，又扛过四个月的反复受挫，才逼得开发商松口，把道路改了道。
直到看见那张改好的地图重新摊开在桌上，居民们心头的怒气才终于平息下来。

passages.title: 回顾展风波
en: For forty years, the ceramic artist had been {{illustrious}} in her small town, praised in every regional museum.
Then a dealer proved {{dishonest}}, caught quietly forging her signature onto fakes he sold as originals.
Her once-loyal patrons proved {{fickle}}, drifting to whichever young sculptor the magazines praised that month.
A new gallery opened across the street, {{flashy}} in its neon signage and marble floors.
Critics still praised her {{sensuous}} glazed curves as the most tactile ceramic work in the region.
A rival curator made {{outrageous}}, baseless claims that her assistants had made every piece she ever signed.
Her own former apprentice, feeling {{resentment}} after years of being overlooked, sided with the rival.
Her testimony felt especially {{disloyal}}, since the sculptor had trained her for free for a decade.
Still, her {{tenacious}} studio manager spent months tracking down scattered ownership records to clear her name.
The dispute with the rival curator turned so {{acrimonious}} that neither would attend the retrospective's opening.
zh: 那位陶艺家在小镇上声名显赫了四十年，作品在附近的博物馆里几乎都展出过。
后来，一个经销商原形毕露——他被当场抓获，一直悄悄仿冒她的签名，把赝品当真品卖了出去。
曾经忠实的收藏家们却见异思迁，谁被杂志捧红就追捧谁。
街对面新开了一家画廊，霓虹招牌配大理石地面，处处花里胡哨，晃得人眼花。
评论家们依然称赞她那些釉色饱满、触感诱人的曲线造型，说是本地最有质感的陶艺作品。
一位对头策展人在媒体上信口雌黄，毫无根据地宣称她的每件作品都是助手代工的。
她曾经的学徒因多年得不到赏识而心怀怨恨，转而支持了那位对头的说法。
这番证词尤其显得忘恩负义，毕竟当年师父白教了她整整十年手艺。
好在她那位锲而不舍的工作室经理花了几个月，四处翻找零散的所有权记录，才替她正了名。
她和那位对头策展人的争执闹得剑拔弩张，回顾展开幕当晚两人谁都没有露面。

passages.title: 书店保卫战
en: When the private equity firm first approached, the founder's daughter {{rebuff|rebuffed}} their offer single-handedly, without a glance.
The tone of the firm's early emails stayed {{bantering}}, as if buying the bookstore were a friendly game.
Board members were quick to {{resent}} the firm's assumption that a lower offer would still be accepted.
Lawyers later learned the firm had {{deceive|deceived}} the family about its plan to shut every store.
The daughter was determined to {{uphold}} her late father's rule: never answer to a chain.
Their accountant found the whole negotiation a deeply {{disagreeable}} task, dreaded every morning.
A local lawyer helped them {{foil}} the firm's plan to buy out three suppliers first.
Staff launched a petition to {{repel}} the takeover as if it were an advancing army, collecting signatures from decades-long regulars.
Their {{tenacious}} founder's daughter spent eight months rallying investors and rewriting the business plan until the firm finally withdrew.
By the end, negotiations had grown so {{acrimonious}} that lawyers exchanged letters instead of speaking.
zh: 私募基金第一次开价时，创始人的女儿只身一人，看都没看就一口回绝了对方的报价。
对方早期邮件的语气始终带着打趣的意味，仿佛收购一家家族书店不过是场游戏。
董事们很快就对这种“降价也照样能成交”的傲慢假设心生不满。
律师后来才发现，那家基金一直在真实计划上蒙骗这家人——他们其实打算一年内关掉每一家门店。
女儿下定决心要恪守父亲的遗训：绝不向连锁集团低头。
会计倒是觉得这场谈判本身就是个苦差事，每天早上都不想面对。
本地律师帮他们挫败了对方暗中收购三家供应商的算盘。
员工发起联署，要把这次收购当成来犯之敌一样挡退，签名的都是光顾了几十年的老顾客。
创始人这位锲而不舍的女儿花了整整八个月拉拢投资人、重写商业计划，最终逼得对方主动撤出。
到最后，双方的谈判闹得剑拔弩张，律师之间只互相寄信，谁也不肯当面开口。

passages.title: 小提琴鉴定风波
en: The old violin's {{plaintive}} tone had haunted the concert hall for a century.
When the family fell {{destitute}} after the war, they quietly listed the instrument for auction.
A dealer fawned over the widow, {{sycophantic}}, hoping she would sell to him alone.
Her {{acquiescence}}, when it came, surprised no one who had watched his relentless flattery.
Establishing the violin's {{provenance}} meant tracing four changes of ownership across two centuries.
Where the ledgers had gaps, the appraiser relied on careful {{interpolation}} between the dated repairs on either side.
A rival expert argued the varnish looked freshly applied, mistaking simple {{recency}} for forgery.
The appraiser who first mislabeled the instrument decades earlier was widely considered {{blameworthy}} for the confusion.
Still, the young researcher was {{tenacious}}, spending a full year cross-checking customs records no one else would touch.
Her dispute with the rival expert grew so {{acrimonious}} that the auction house barred them from the same room.
zh: 那把旧小提琴哀婉的音色，在音乐厅里回荡了整整一个世纪。
战后家道中落，一家人悄悄把这把琴送去拍卖行。
一个经销商围着寡妇献殷勤、谄媚讨好，指望她只肯卖给自己。
她最终点头应允，没人感到意外，大家都看着他这几个月殷勤讨好。
要查清这把琴的来历，得理清两百年间四次易主的产权变迁。
账本上有缺口的地方，鉴定师就靠着前后维修记录做审慎的插值推算来填补。
一位对手专家却认定清漆太新，仅凭这份新近，就一口咬定是伪造的铁证。
几十年前第一个给这把琴贴错标签的鉴定师，普遍被认为该为这场混乱负责。
好在这位年轻的研究员锲而不舍，花了整整一年翻查别人都懒得碰的海关记录。
她和那位对手专家的争执闹得剑拔弩张，拍卖行最后干脆不让两人同处一室。

passages.title: 湖边小屋周末
en: The old photographs on the mantel felt almost unbearably {{evocative}}, pulling everyone back to summers long past.
Every {{reminiscence}} ended with someone laughing about their father's terrible fishing stories.
Then the spring storm proved {{disastrous}}, tearing the dock clean off its posts overnight.
Their cousin, ever {{ingenious}}, rebuilt half the dock from planks the storm had ripped loose.
Whether the family could still {{hold-together|hold together}} once their father was gone was the weekend's real question.
Their aunt kept the conversation {{coherent}}, steering it away from decades-old grudges each time one surfaced.
By Sunday, no one in the house was entirely {{untroubled}}, though everyone pretended otherwise for their aunt.
Still, watching the dock stand again by sunset left the cousin genuinely {{fulfilled}}.
Only their {{tenacious}} aunt kept pushing, weekend after weekend, until the house was finally taken off the market.
The argument over selling turned so {{acrimonious}} that two cousins didn't speak again until spring.
zh: 壁炉台上的那些老照片格外勾人回忆，一下子把所有人拽回了那些以为早就忘记的夏天。
每次追忆往事，总会有人笑着提起父亲那些编得离谱的钓鱼故事。
谁知那场春天的风暴闹出了大祸，一夜之间就把码头从桩子上整个掀翻。
表哥向来鬼点子多，硬是用风暴卷落的那些木板，把码头修回了一半。
父亲走后，这个家还能不能凝聚在一起，成了这个周末真正要面对的问题。
姑姑一直设法让谈话保持条理，每次快扯到几十年的旧账就赶紧把话题岔开。
到了周日，屋里其实没人真正心里踏实，只是大家都在姑姑面前装出若无其事的样子。
可看着码头在夕阳下重新立起来，表哥还是打心眼里觉得这事干得值。
全靠姑姑锲而不舍，一个周末接一个周末地坚持，房子才终于从待售名单上撤了下来。
这场该不该卖房子的争吵闹得剑拔弩张，两个表亲从此谁也不理谁，直到来年春天才又开口。

passages.title: 家族酒庄的债务
en: Marco inherited the vineyard and was famously {{profligate}}, replacing good oak barrels every season just because he liked the smell.
His sister Elena was {{sagacious}} enough to warn him for years the debts would catch up with him.
The dinner argument only {{aggravate|aggravated}} months of simmering tension between them.
Even so, they stayed oddly {{like-minded}} about one thing: neither wanted investors touching the land.
Investors circled, but every pitch meeting stayed {{lukewarm}}, the suits nodding politely and never calling back.
Only Priya, a stranger from a tasting, was {{affable}} enough to offer to check the books for free.
She proved {{zealous}} about the audit, double-checking every invoice even after Marco begged her to stop.
Despite the grim numbers, she stayed stubbornly {{upbeat}}, certain one good harvest could turn things around.
Elena's {{tenacious}} pursuit of refinancing — three banks in three months — finally saved the estate.
The last real fight was {{acrimonious}}, Marco and his uncle trading blame over the label design.
zh: 马可继承了家族酒庄，出了名的花钱大手大脚：明明橡木桶还好好的，他也要每季一换，就因为喜欢新木头的气味。
他姐姐埃琳娜很有远见，多年前就提醒过他，账单迟早会找上门。
晚饭时旧事重提，那场争执反倒让本就紧绷的姐弟关系火上浇油。
尽管如此，两人在一件事上出奇地想法一致：谁都不想让外面的投资人插手这片地。
投资人倒是来了不少，可每次洽谈都反应平平，那些西装革履的人礼貌点头，之后再没了下文。
只有普丽娅——品酒会上遇见的一位陌生人——为人和善，主动提出要免费帮忙查账。
没想到她查起账来近乎狂热，连马可求她别查了，她还是把每张发票核对了两遍。
尽管数字很难看，她还是一副乐观劲儿，坚信只要有一年好收成，一切就能翻盘。
真正救了这片庄园的，是埃琳娜的锲而不舍——三个月里跑了三家银行，才终于有一家答应重新贷款。
最后一场真正的争吵闹得不欢而散，马可和叔叔为了酒标该印谁的名字互相指责。

passages.title: 老楼维修风波
en: Rosa's {{frankness}} startled the others: the landlord, she said, had let it rot on purpose.
Doug from 2A was famously {{quarrelsome}}, fighting with neighbors over parking spots and recycling bins.
The new manager showed real {{receptiveness}}, reading the maintenance log tenants had kept for years.
The engineer's report made repairs look {{insurmountable}}: rewiring, re-roofing, foundation work the fund could never cover.
Rosa suspected something {{wicked}}, not neglect: corners cut on purpose to drive out tenants and flip the building for profit.
A tip from a city inspector was {{timely}}, catching the landlord mid-renovation, gutting apartments without permits.
His lawyer threatened to {{litigate}} against the tenants' association for defamation over Rosa's comments.
In the basement, a crack curled back on itself, {{sinuous}} and snake-like, along the foundation wall.
Rosa proved {{tenacious}}, filing the same request on three separate occasions before an inspector finally showed up.
The final meeting turned {{acrimonious}}, both sides trading accusations until the manager called the police.
zh: 罗莎的坦率让所有人都愣住了——她直言不讳地说，房东是故意放任这栋楼烂下去的。
2A的道格出了名地爱抬杠，为了车位和分类垃圾桶的事能跟邻居吵个没完。
新来的物业经理真心愿意听意见，把住户们记了两年的维修日志一条条看了下来。
工程师的报告一出来，维修账单大得让人绝望：电路、屋顶、地基全要重做，住户的公积金根本不够填。
罗莎怀疑这背后不只是疏于管理，而是蓄意为之：故意偷工减料，把受租金管制的住户逼走，转手把楼卖个好价钱。
一条来自市检查员的线索来得正是时候，让人当场撞见房东在没有许可证的情况下私自翻修公寓。
房东的律师扬言要以诽谤为由把住户协会告上法庭。
地下室里，一道蜿蜒的裂缝像蛇一样一圈圈绕着，顺着地基墙延伸开去。
罗莎却锲而不舍，同一份申请连递了三次，直到最后一位检查员终于上门。
最后一次见面彻底闹翻，双方隔着桌子互相指责，直到物业经理报警。

passages.title: 造假丑闻
en: Dr. Halvorsen had once been {{celebrated}} as the brightest mind of his generation.
It later emerged that plain {{deceit}} ran through his results: control groups invented from nothing.
Elena, his visually {{impaired}} lab partner, first noticed two different experiments sharing identical, suspicious numbers.
When reporters reached him, he grew {{evasive}}, steering every question back to unrelated papers.
His graduate students grew {{anxious}}, unsure whether their own names would drag their careers down with his.
One postdoc, Mara, chose to {{oppose}} him publicly, filing a formal complaint instead of staying quiet.
Within a week, the funding body {{rescind|rescinded}} the grant that had built his laboratory.
The inquiry also revealed a quieter {{impairment}}: for years a hidden hearing loss had made him miss half of what students told him.
Only Mara stayed {{tenacious}}, filing the same records request three times before the ministry finally complied.
The final hearing turned {{acrimonious}}, Halvorsen and Mara trading accusations until the chair cut off the session.
zh: 哈尔沃森博士曾是公认那一代最聪明的头脑，奖项拿到手软。
后来才发现，他发表的成果里满是彻头彻尾的造假：好几组所谓的对照实验根本从未做过，数据全是凭空编出来的。
他那位视力不太好的实验室搭档埃琳娜最先发现，两个号称不同的实验，用的却是一模一样、准确得可疑的数字。
记者堵到他时，他开始顾左右而言他，每次都把话题绕回团队其他不相干的论文上。
他的研究生们人人自危，不知道自己署名的论文会不会把自己也一起拖下水。
博士后玛拉是唯一站出来公开反对他的人，没有像其他人那样沉默，而是正式提交了投诉。
不到一周，资助机构就撤销了当初撑起他整间实验室的那笔经费。
调查还揭出另一件隐情：多年来他一直瞒着自己的听力障碍，学生说的话他有一半根本没听清。
只有玛拉锲而不舍，同一份档案申请连递了三次，直到部里终于批复。
最后那场听证会不欢而散，哈尔沃森和玛拉互相指责，最后是主席叫停才结束。

passages.title: 山中寺院的骗局
en: The old abbot practiced a strict {{asceticism}}, sleeping on bare boards and living on rice and water.
The newest acolyte was comically {{obsequious}}, bowing three times before every meal.
Months passed before anyone noticed the {{trickery}}: donation boxes relabeled, coins skimmed before the count.
Tenzin, the youngest monk, noticed it first but said nothing, his usual {{diffidence}} silencing him.
A quiet {{disaffection}} spread instead, monks skipping his prayer shifts without ever saying why.
Outside, the crowd of pilgrims grew more {{clamorous}} by the week, drawn by rumors he read omens in the clouds.
He claimed a red sunset would {{portend}} a harsh winter, and charged pilgrims for the warning.
When questioned, he would {{ramble}} about signs and spirits until listeners forgot the question.
Tenzin finally grew {{tenacious}}, checking the ledger three nights running even after being told to stop, until the coins added up.
The confrontation was {{acrimonious}}, the acolyte shouting until the abbot ordered him off the mountain.
zh: 老方丈苦修极严，睡的是光板床，吃的只有米饭和清水。
新来的小沙弥谄媚得近乎滑稽，每顿饭前都要拜上三拜，句句奉承。
过了好几个月，才有人看出他这份虔诚背后的猫腻：功德箱的标签被悄悄换过，点数之前钱已经被他抽走一部分。
最年轻的僧人丹增最先察觉不对，却什么也没说——他生性怯懦，不敢开口指控一位师兄。
取而代之的是寺里悄悄蔓延开的离心：僧人们开始无声无息地躲开他当值的祈祷班次，谁也不说原因。
山门外，聚拢的香客一周比一周吵闹，都是听说他能从云相里看出预兆而赶来的。
他扬言脊岭上的一抹晚霞预示着严冬将至，还借着这警示向香客收钱。
一被人追问，他就能扯着神迹鬼怪东拉西扯上一个钟头，问的人早忘了自己问的是什么。
丹增终于横下心来，一连三晚查对账本，哪怕一位老僧劝他别再查了也不肯罢手，直到那笔对不上的钱终于凑齐了。
随后的对质闹得很凶，那沙弥一路嚷嚷着说自己受了委屈，方丈当场下令让他离开山门。

passages.title: 指挥家的告别演出季
en: Maestro Yuen had been the {{foremost}} conductor for thirty years, but this season felt different.
Insomnia kept him {{restless}} most nights, his mind replaying old performances instead of sleep.
His pupil Mei was refreshingly {{forthright}}: she told him plainly his tempos had gone slack.
The next review proved even more {{devastating}}, calling the orchestra a shadow of itself.
As if on cue, the council {{enact|enacted}} a noise ordinance that week, threatening the courtyard rehearsals.
Yet the final rehearsal, the night before the ordinance took effect, felt oddly {{serene}}.
Mei had been {{tenacious}} about that passage for weeks, three bowings tried and abandoned, until it locked together.
Backstage, Yuen admitted his thirty years now felt like near {{insignificance}} beside what Mei would build next.
She told him the goodbye was at least {{bearable}}, knowing whose hands the orchestra would fall into.
Only two board members arguing over the encore turned {{acrimonious}}, trading blame until Yuen stepped in.
zh: 袁指挥在这个地区当了三十年首屈一指的指挥家，但这最后一个演出季感觉格外不同。
那年春天，他大半夜里都因失眠而辗转难安，脑子里翻来覆去全是从前演出的画面。
他最得意的学生梅一向说话直来直去：她当面告诉他，节奏已经松垮了。
第二天早上的乐评更狠，语气近乎毁灭性，直说乐团如今只剩当年的影子。
仿佛是故意凑热闹，市议会就在同一周通过了一项噪音法令，威胁到乐团一直免费使用的庭院排练。
可就在法令生效前一晚，最后一次庭院排练却出奇地宁静安详，弦乐声一点点归位。
梅为了那一小段乐句较了好几周的劲，换了三种运弓法都不满意，直到那个声部终于合在了一起。
后台里，袁指挥坦言自己这三十年，比起梅日后要做的事，忽然显得微不足道。
她对他说，至少现在这场告别还算撑得下去，因为她清楚乐团接下来会交到谁手里。
唯独两位理事为返场曲目争执起来，在后台互相指责，直到袁指挥出面才劝住。

passages.title: 小镇合同揭露
en: The clerk who filed it was {{unwary}}, signing an altered budget line without noticing the total had changed.
Reporter Mei stayed {{assiduous}}, poring over eight years of council minutes until a pattern emerged.
The motive was almost comic: the facilities chief was a well-known {{epicure}}, and the skimmed money bought his private dinners.
The {{machination}} was simple: inflate the estimate, then bury the difference in a maintenance line.
The newsroom went {{agog}} the moment Mei walked in, desperate to know what she'd found.
His {{discursive}} testimony at the hearing wandered from the contract to boat repairs to a neighbor dispute.
Mei's headline was {{felicitous}}: two words that captured the scheme without one challengeable accusation.
The meeting turned {{acrimonious}} within minutes, neighbors who'd shared potlucks for years shouting across the chairs.
Three reporters before her had quit, but Mei stayed {{tenacious}} until a retired clerk agreed to talk.
The councilman spent months after on a slow {{extrication}} from every committee he'd once chaired.
zh: 负责归档的办事员并不警觉，在被悄悄改动过两次的预算项上签了字，浑然不觉总数早已不对。
记者小梅对这条线索格外用心，一头扎进八年的议会会议记录里，直到一个可疑的模式渐渐浮现。
动机说来近乎荒唐：那位设施主管竟是个远近闻名的美食家，贪没的公款全砸在了他私下的饭局里。
这笔交易背后的手法堪称精巧：先虚报预算，再把差额悄悄藏进一条维修开支里。
小梅一走进编辑部，整间办公室都热切地围了上来，都想在稿子见报前先知道她挖出了什么。
听证会上，设施主管的证词东拉西扯，从合同本身扯到他家船的维修，又扯到跟邻居的纠纷。
小梅的标题起得恰到好处：短短几个字就点出了整个骗局，市长的律师却挑不出一句可指控的话。
会议很快就变得剑拔弩张，往年一起办烧烤聚会的邻居们，此刻隔着折叠椅互相吼了起来。
在她之前的三位记者都半途而废，小梅却锲而不舍，直到一位早已退休的办事员终于开了口。
那位议员接下来几个月都在从他曾主持过的每个委员会里艰难脱身，一个接一个地辞去席位。

passages.title: 家族面包店的风波
en: When Daniel proposed a third bakery, Grace called it {{overambitious}} — the second shop still wasn't profitable.
Their father's health had entered a slow {{deterioration}}, and the shop's finances were no steadier.
Grace learned their father had been {{unfaithful}} for years, meeting another woman every Tuesday.
That dinner turned {{acrimonious}} instantly, their mother's usual silence breaking into something nobody could take back.
Their aunt, ever {{tactful}}, steered later gatherings away from the affair before anyone noticed the shift.
Grace still felt a lingering {{discomfort}} at her father's small talk.
She stayed {{tenacious}} about keeping the shop open, arriving at five every morning through months of silence.
Their savings had {{lessened}} by nearly half after their father's medical bills, leaving little for Daniel's plan.
Only the accountant's numbers finally showed the real {{magnitude}} of the second shop's debt — nearly triple what anyone had guessed.
Their mother's response held a real {{subtlety}} — not forgiveness, just a small, deliberate softening.
zh: 丹尼尔提议开第三家店时，姐姐格蕾丝说这未免好高骛远，第二家店都还没赚到钱呢。
那一年，父亲的身体每况愈下，店里的财务状况也没好到哪去。
格蕾丝发现父亲多年来一直对母亲不忠，每周二都借口见供应商，实则去会另一个女人。
她把这事说出口的那顿晚饭，气氛瞬间剑拔弩张，母亲一贯的隐忍在那一刻彻底崩塌，再也收不回去。
姑姑向来很会把握分寸，此后每次家庭聚会一提到那件事，她总能不动声色地把话题岔开。
父亲每次跟她闲聊店里的事，格蕾丝心里仍会泛起一阵说不清的别扭，仿佛两人之间什么都没发生过。
尽管如此，她还是咬牙坚持要留住那家老店，哪怕家人几个月都互不说话，她照样每天五点开门。
付完父亲的医药费，家里的积蓄少了将近一半，丹尼尔的扩张计划几乎没了着落。
直到会计把账目摊开，大家才真正意识到第二家店欠下的债有多庞大。
母亲最终的反应里带着一种微妙的分寸——算不上原谅，只是一种刻意的、悄悄的软化。

passages.title: 酒庄合伙人纠纷
en: For years, Owen ran the tasting room {{contented}}, wanting nothing more than his grandfather's forty acres.
Reyes grew {{dismissive}} of Owen's caution, waving off budget concerns without glancing at the spreadsheet.
Reyes quietly financed a new pavilion — marble, imported fixtures — pure {{extravagance}} eating two years of profit.
Owen saw the receipts and accused Reyes of trying to {{defame}} him to investors with a false story.
Their shouting match was startlingly {{acrimonious}} for two men who'd built the company without a single fight.
A lawyer suggested {{conciliation}} first, a neutral facilitator getting both men to talk without demands.
They then agreed to binding {{arbitration}}, bound by contract to accept the panel's decision.
It was Owen's daughter, far more {{enlightened}} about modern co-ownership terms, who drafted the settlement.
Nobody had planned her involvement; it was an entirely {{spontaneous}} dinner offer that became three weeks of drafting.
She stayed {{tenacious}} through every late-night call, refusing to let the deal collapse.
zh: 多年来，欧文一直安于打理酒庄的品鉴室，别无所求，守着祖父留下的那四十英亩地就心满意足。
他的合伙人雷耶斯却越来越不把欧文的谨慎当回事，账单看都不看就把预算上的顾虑一挥而过。
雷耶斯背着人出资建了座新品鉴馆，大理石台面、进口灯具，这番挥霍两年利润都填不满。
欧文看到账单后，反被雷耶斯倒打一耙，说他在投资人面前散布谣言，诬称是欧文自己批准的开支——纯属捏造。
两个一起把公司做起来、从没红过脸的人，那场争吵竟吵得剑拔弩张，谁都不肯让谁。
律师建议先试试调解——找个中立的人把两人拉到一个房间里谈，谁也不用先提条件。
调解不了了之后，两人转而同意交由仲裁裁定，并签字约定必须服从裁决结果，不得反悔。
出人意料的是，最终起草和解条款的，是欧文那位刚毕业的女儿——她对现代合伙协议的理解开明得多。
谁也没料到她会插手，那不过是某次晚饭桌上一时兴起的提议，后来却变成了三周字斟句酌的起草工作。
面对两位父辈深更半夜打来的电话，她始终锲而不舍，哪怕双方都撂过狠话要退出，她也没让这桩交易黄掉。

passages.title: 乐团数据选曲风波
en: When the festival hired a new director, he built a fully {{probabilistic}} model for predicting sales.
The safest scores it recommended were the most {{melodious}} ones on record, hummed for decades.
A board member warned the committee, in terms everyone found {{credible}}, that repetition would empty seats.
{{notwithstanding}} the warning, the board approved it, and musicians soon felt reduced to a formula.
Ticket-holders' {{dissatisfaction}} showed up in the comment cards — not anger, just a shrug.
The director's old mentor hadn't spoken to him since, and the {{estrangement}} between them only grew colder.
By spring, the recording contract — {{assignable}} to any platform under an old agreement — sparked new conflict.
Under pressure, the director quietly {{backslide|backslid}} into programming by instinct, restoring pieces the model had rejected.
The meeting turned {{acrimonious}} at once, two men who'd traded only nods for years now shouting.
Even so, the director stayed {{tenacious}} about the data-driven approach, refusing to scrap two years of work.
zh: 音乐节请来新任指挥后，他建了一套概率模型，排练还没开始，就能预测每首曲子的票房。
模型推荐的最保险的曲目，毫不意外全是最悦耳动听的那几首——听众哼了几十年的老调子。
一位理事出言警告，说法令全体委员都深信不疑：曲目年年雷同，比任何一篇差评更能让剧场空掉。
尽管有这番警告，理事会还是批准了这套模型，短短几个月，一半乐手都觉得自己被简化成了一道公式。
观众的不满最先反映在意见卡上，倒也算不上愤怒，只是一种对曲目太好猜的失望和摇头。
指挥的老恩师自模型公布以来就没再跟他说过话，两人之间的疏远只是越拖越冷。
到了春天，那份录音合同——按多年前双方签下的条款，可转让给任何一家流媒体平台——成了新一轮争执的焦点。
顶不住压力，指挥又悄悄故态复萌，凭直觉排曲子，把模型否掉的曲目又悄悄加了回去。
合同纠纷浮出水面的那场会议瞬间火药味十足，两个十年来见面只点头致意的人突然扯着嗓子吵了起来。
尽管如此，指挥仍执意保留部分数据选曲的做法，不肯因一个糟糕的乐季就放弃两年的心血。

passages.title: 仓库旺季风波
en: Every December, the manager tried to get {{proactive}}, adding loaders weeks before the rush.
Even so, a low {{anticipatory}} dread settled over the floor every year around Thanksgiving.
The scanner that failed twice a shift had become a running {{annoyance}}, the kind nobody bothered reporting.
Owen's {{irritation}} was something else — the same broken cart for six days had him barely keeping calm.
Priya, always more {{solitary}} than the crew, took the graveyard shift on purpose.
She noticed a small {{nuance}} in the new software: a dropdown that silently reset priority flags.
{{in-spite-of|In spite of}} that bug costing two days of misrouted packages, corporate refused to delay it.
Management responded by getting the desk {{augmented}} with four temporary staff from the call center.
Owen's meeting with his supervisor turned {{acrimonious}}, two coworkers who shared lunch daily now avoiding each other.
Priya stayed {{tenacious}} about the bug, filing the same ticket four times after each silent closure.
zh: 每年十二月，班组长都想未雨绸缪，提前几周就多加两名装卸工，而不是等第一波积压出现了才反应。
即便如此，每年一到感恩节前后，仓库里都会弥漫起一种隐隐的、提前到来的焦躁，连加派的卡车都还没影儿。
那台每班总要掉线两次的扫码枪，成了新人们心照不宣的小麻烦，大家嘴上抱怨几句，却没人真去报修。
欧文的烦躁却完全是另一回事——同一辆坏推车用了整整六天，还没到中午，他的声音就快压不住了。
普丽娅一向比组里其他人更独来独往，故意挑了大夜班，三条空荡荡的通道，连个说话的人都没有。
她注意到新物流软件里一个不起眼的细节：一个下拉菜单会悄悄重置国际订单的优先级标记。
尽管那个漏洞已经害仓库错发了整整两天的包裹，总部还是不肯把上线计划往后推。
管理层的应对是从楼下客服中心临时调来四个人，把支援团队充实了一番。
欧文终于当面质问主管的那场碰头会瞬间火药味十足，两个平时天天一起吃午饭的同事，突然谁也不看谁一眼。
普丽娅却锲而不舍，非要把那个下拉菜单的漏洞彻底修好，工单被莫名其妙关掉四次，她就重新提交四次。

passages.title: 船坞里的修复
en: Their uncle loved to {{disparage}} the boat's crooked seams, sneering that a child could plane straighter wood.
The old shipwright had been hired to {{superintend}} the yard's work, checking each seam before high tide.
His {{manifold}} duties — logging tides, rationing tar, settling squabbles — left him no time to rest.
The yard's access channel stayed {{winding}}, forcing every delivery barge to idle through its bends.
He preferred to {{reprove}} apprentices quietly, never with the harsh rebukes older sailors still remembered.
Bribing the inspector to overlook a cracked frame felt {{repugnant}}, though the money would have helped.
Steaming each rib into shape proved {{laborious}}, a process that swallowed most of the summer.
His grip on the clamp stayed {{tenacious}}, fingers refusing to loosen even as they went numb.
When the committee argued over mooring fees, the debate turned {{acrimonious}}, friends shouting across the table.
When the boat passed inspection, the harbor-master gave it his {{approbation}} with an approving nod.
zh: 叔叔总爱当着路人的面贬低这条船歪斜的接缝，冷嘲说随便找个孩子来刨木头都比这齐整。
老船匠受雇监管船坞的日常事务，涨潮前总要把每道接缝检查一遍。
他要操心的事林林总总——记录潮汐、分配沥青、平息小争执——忙得连坐下歇口气的工夫都没有。
通往船坞的水道蜿蜒曲折，逼得每艘运货驳船都得减速绕行。
他更愿意心平气和地教训学徒，从不像老水手们记忆中那种劈头盖脸的斥责。
贿赂检查员放过一道裂缝的念头让他反感，尽管那笔钱本能解他的燃眉之急。
把每根船肋蒸弯定型十分费时费力——这道工序耗掉了大半个夏天。
他死死抓住夹钳不松手，手指冻得发麻也不肯放开。
委员会为停泊费吵起来时，场面变得剑拔弩张，老朋友们隔着桌子互相叫嚷。
船最终通过验收时，港务长只点了点头表示认可，别无他话。

passages.title: 外交官的冬日手记
en: Short, {{gloomy}} December days pressed against the cottage windows, the sun barely clearing the ridge.
He had chosen this {{solitude}} gladly after forty years abroad; the quiet no longer felt lonely.
Each morning he sorted boxes of old {{diplomatic}} cables from his Foreign Service years for the memoir.
One brittle 1961 dispatch recorded {{benighted}} local beliefs about a comet that had cursed the harbor.
After an hour of silent {{cogitation}} over the evening's chess problem, he finally saw the mate in three.
March itself passed almost entirely {{uneventful}}, the terrier's woodpile raid the only interruption.
That terrier greeted every visitor with {{exuberant}} barking and leaping that rattled the teacups.
He felt briefly {{euphoric}} the afternoon a chapter came together, though the feeling faded by dinner.
The ivy on the chimney stayed {{tenacious}}, creeping back through the mortar every spring despite his weeding.
A phone call from home about selling the family house turned {{acrimonious}} before he could say hello.
zh: 十二月的白昼又短又阴沉，天色刚爬过山脊便又暗了下来，终日压在小屋的窗玻璃上。
独居这些年是他心甘情愿选的，侨居国外四十年后，如今的清静再也不让他觉得孤单。
每天早上，他都要翻检当年在外交部工作时留下的一箱箱旧电报，挑出能写进回忆录的那些。
其中一份1961年的脆黄电报，记录着当地人愚昧地相信一颗彗星给港口带来了诅咒。
对着当晚的一道棋局苦思冥想了一个钟头，他才终于看出三步将死的杀招。
三月几乎风平浪静地过去了，唯一的插曲是那只㹴犬刨翻了柴堆。
那只㹴犬倒是活力四射，逮着谁来串门就又叫又扑，把茶杯震得叮当响。
那天下午一章稿子终于写顺了，他一度欣喜若狂，只是这股劲头到晚饭时就已经散了。
烟囱上的常春藤格外顽强，任他每年春天怎么拔，它总能顺着灰缝钻回来。
一通商量卖掉老宅的电话，他刚打完招呼，气氛就已经剑拔弩张。

passages.title: 酒庄继承人
en: The heir's {{profligacy}} with the harvest money — sommeliers flown in for a week-long party — left the vineyard drowning in debt.
His plan to save the business depended on three unlikely things happening at once, a scheme his lawyer called {{far-fetched}}.
The bottling machine was simply {{unfixable}}; the mechanic ordered a replacement.
But the damage to the family's name in the valley felt {{irremediable}}, past any apology.
Even the cousins who despised him still spoke {{respectful|respectfully}} of their grandfather's original vines.
At dinner, his aunt was openly {{contemptuous}}, reading his wine-tasting notes aloud in a mocking voice.
His uncle said nothing, sweeping past {{disdainful|disdainfully}} and never sitting down.
The lawyer's knowing little smile was {{suggestive}} of debts nobody had mentioned yet.
Only the oldest vine on the hill stayed {{tenacious}}, its roots too deep to dig out.
The family meeting that followed turned {{acrimonious}} within minutes, decades of grudges spilling onto the table.
zh: 这位继承人挥霍无度——光是从意大利请侍酒师来撑一场办了一周的派对，就花掉了整季葡萄的收成——酒庄很快就债台高筑。
他那套救急方案得指望三件不太可能的事同时凑巧发生，连自家律师都说这个主意牵强得很。
装瓶机倒是没什么好说的，彻底报废了，修理工看都不看直接叫他换新的。
但酒庄的名声在整个山谷里跌得实在太狠，怎么道歉都补不回来了。
就连那些瞧不起他的堂表兄弟，提起祖父当年亲手栽下的那批老藤，语气也还是恭恭敬敬的。
晚饭时，姑姑当众冷嘲热讽，把他写的品酒笔记大声念出来，念得阴阳怪气。
叔叔倒是一言不发，只是不屑地从品酒室门口扫过，连座都没坐。
律师那意味深长的笑，暗示着还有一笔谁都没提过的债。
山坡上唯有那棵最老的葡萄藤依旧顽强，根扎得太深，谁也挖不动。
随后召开的家庭会议没几分钟就吵翻了天，几十年的积怨全摊到了桌面上。

passages.title: 灯会风波
en: {{relentless}} rain fell on the lantern festival for six straight days, never once letting up.
The festival's elderly organizer grew increasingly {{cranky}}, snapping at any volunteer who asked him a question twice.
The youngest volunteer stayed {{stoic}}, standing soaked at her post without complaint.
Then, the night before opening, the main generator's failure proved {{untimely}}, and it refused to restart.
Old Chen's grip on the ladder stayed {{tenacious}} as the wind tried to shake him loose, thirty feet above the crowd.
The town official assigned to {{oversee}} gate safety missed the whole dragon mix-up, too busy arguing with the generator repairman.
The mix-up was {{perplexing}}: half the paper dragons arrived at the wrong gate entirely.
If the rain counted as bad luck, {{by-the-same-token}}, so did the missing dragons.
Despite everything, the festival still featured {{prominently}} on the regional paper's front page next morning.
The volunteer meeting afterward turned {{acrimonious}}, everyone blaming everyone else for the runaway budget.
zh: 连着六天，雨下得没完没了，把整个灯会都泡在了水里。
灯会的老会长脾气越来越差，谁要是把一句话问上两遍，他就没好气地怼回去。
最年轻的志愿者倒是稳得住，浑身淋透地守在岗位上，一句抱怨也没有。
谁知开幕前一晚，主发电机的故障偏偏来得不是时候，说什么也发动不起来。
老陈扒着梯子死死不撒手，风一个劲儿地想把他从三十英尺高的架子上掀下来。
镇上派来监督入口安全的官员完全没顾上纸龙灯的乌龙，正忙着跟发电机维修工吵架。
这场乌龙让人摸不着头脑：一半的纸龙灯全都送错了门。
如果说这场雨算是倒霉，那照这个理儿，纸龙灯送错地方也一样是倒霉。
尽管如此，第二天早上，灯会还是上了地方报纸的头版，位置显眼。
事后的志愿者例会很快就吵翻了，人人都把预算失控归咎到别人头上。

passages.title: 彗星乌龙
en: His {{purported}} comet discovery lit up the forum within hours of the post.
He had long wanted {{preeminence}} among the forum's stargazers, and this felt like his chance.
His method was {{ostensibly}} rigorous, three nights of coordinates logged and cross-checked against the star atlas.
The real {{imprudence}} was posting before anyone outside his own backyard had confirmed a single measurement.
One retired physics teacher went digging for her old star charts, prying open a drawer that stayed {{tenacious|tenaciously}} stuck.
What she found made the correction {{humiliating}} — the comet was just a cataloged asteroid, misread.
The retraction thread left him {{alienated}} from a community he had posted in nightly for six years.
The moderators, meanwhile, answered questions about the mess with barely concealed {{exasperation}}.
His increasingly defensive replies only {{agitate|agitated}} longtime members already worried about the forum's reputation.
By the weekend, the whole thread had turned {{acrimonious}}, old friendships fraying over one wrong number.
zh: 他自称发现了一颗新彗星，帖子刚发出去没几个小时，整个业余天文论坛就炸开了锅。
他一直渴望在论坛的观星圈子里出人头地，这回感觉终于等来了机会。
他的方法表面上看挺严谨——连续三晚记录坐标，还对照星图反复核对过。
真正轻率的地方在于，他后院之外根本没人核实过一个数据，他就贸然发了帖。
一位退休的物理老师翻箱倒柜找她当年的星图，那个抽屉死活拉不开，她使出全身力气才把它掰开。
结果发现的东西让这场更正颜面尽失：所谓的彗星不过是他看错了的一颗已编目小行星。
撤帖引发的那串回复，把他和这个他泡了整整六年的论坛社区生生隔开了。
版主们疲于应付各种质疑，语气里藏不住的都是不耐烦。
他越描越黑的辩解，只让本就担心论坛名声的老会员们更加心烦意乱。
到了周末，整个帖子已经吵成一团，老交情都为了一个数字上的失误闹掰了。

passages.title: 码头条例风波
en: Every spring the clerk turned {{officious}}, checking boat-slip records nobody had asked her to check.
This year she found real trouble: the pier's planks had gone {{treacherous}}, rot hidden under fresh paint.
The dock manager had been {{deceitful}} for months, telling the board the boards were sound.
The mayor's reply was {{understated}}: a plain notice on the board, nothing more.
Behind it sat a town {{ordinance}} the council had passed years earlier and never enforced.
She read the {{proclamation}} aloud on the steps: every private dock would be inspected by June.
Word spread he'd pocketed repair money too, a scheme fishermen called {{detestable}} long before the audit.
At the meeting he sat {{motionless}}, jaw tightening at each accusation but never once shifting his seat.
Only one reporter stayed {{tenacious}}, filing requests for two years after her editor first spiked the story.
By the vote, the debate had turned so {{acrimonious}} that two members stopped speaking for months.
zh: 每到春天，那位文书就变得格外好管闲事，连没人托她核对的船位记录也要一一过问。
今年她真查出了麻烦：老码头的木板已经暗藏凶险，朽烂之处全藏在新刷的漆下面，一脚踩上去才现形。
码头主管为此欺瞒了理事会好几个月，一口咬定木板没事，其实压根没去看过一眼。
市长的回应很低调：布告栏上贴了张素朴的通知，仅此而已，没开记者会。
通知背后是理事会多年前就通过、却从没真正执行过的一项镇级条例。
她在台阶上当众宣读了公告：入夏前，每一处私人码头都要接受检查。
传言说他还私吞了修缮款，渔民们早在审计结果出来之前就骂这事可憎。
听证会上他一动不动地坐着，每被指控一次下颌就绷紧一分，可身子始终没挪半分。
只有一位记者始终锲而不舍，编辑两年前就把稿子毙了，她还是一直申请查阅记录。
等到表决那天，争论已经激烈到两名理事此后好几个月都互不搭理。

passages.title: 寺院吊桥往事
en: The oldest monk chased {{enlightenment}} for sixty years, rising before dawn in the cold hall.
He lived a spare, {{ascetic}} life: rice once a day, no bed, nothing beyond what he needed.
Visitors swore he seemed almost {{sapient}}, as though he understood things nobody had taught him.
That week brought a more {{exigent}} problem: the footbridge over the ravine had collapsed.
The engineer inspecting the cables blamed {{torsion}}, the twisting strain that had worn through the steel.
The path split at a stone marker, a genuine {{bifurcation}} nobody had ever signposted.
The younger monks and the builders fell into a deeply {{acrimonious}} row over who should pay.
For days the abbot tried to {{conciliate}} both sides, though neither would give an inch.
Asked to explain the dispute, he answered with such {{circumlocution}} that nobody understood a word.
Still he stayed {{tenacious}}, returning to the talks every evening until both sides signed the same page.
zh: 寺里最年长的僧人参悟了六十年，每天天不亮就起身，在寒冷的大殿里打坐。
他过着清苦的日子：一天一碗米饭，不睡床铺，除了必需之物什么都不留。
见过他的人都说他仿佛有种超凡的智慧，好像懂得一些从没人教过他的道理。
可那一周出了件更紧迫的事：峡谷上的那座吊桥刚刚塌了。
来查看钢索的工程师说是扭力惹的祸——常年的扭转应力早把老钢索磨穿了。
小路在一块石碑处分岔，这个岔口几十年来都没人立过路牌。
与此同时，年轻僧人和施工队为修缮费该由谁出，吵得不可开交，火气一天比一天大。
方丈一连数日想从中调解，可谁也不肯让步。
每当有人请他把纠纷说清楚，他总是拐弯抹角一大通，谁也没听懂一句。
尽管如此，他还是锲而不舍，每晚都回去接着谈，直到双方终于在同一份文件上签了字。

passages.title: 后厨翻身记
en: After twenty exhausting years, the owner finally felt real {{contentment}}: a full room, no debts, nothing left to prove.
The new sous-chef had real {{competence}}: nothing flashy, every ticket done correctly and on time.
The summer intern, by contrast, was hopelessly {{inept}}, ruining three sauces in one Friday service.
He was {{deferential}} to the head chef, waiting for a nod before touching any pan.
That July the kitchen's heat turned {{unbearable}}, and two cooks fainted before the ovens were fixed.
The health inspector called the walk-in's wiring {{intolerable}} and closed the kitchen until it was repaired.
The tasting menu's plainest dish was also its most {{deceptive}}: three ingredients that somehow tasted like ten.
One cook, fired that spring, grew {{vengeful}} and began leaving one-star reviews under fake names.
Even so, the owner stayed {{tenacious}}, answering every review by hand for a month straight.
The dispute with the landlord turned {{acrimonious}} before both sides settled in court.
zh: 熬过二十年起早贪黑的日子，老板终于尝到了真正的满足：餐厅坐满，账目清零，再没什么要证明的了。
新来的副主厨很称职：不出风头，每一张单子都按时准确地做完。
相比之下，那个暑期实习生笨手笨脚得没法看，一个周五晚上就毁了三份酱汁。
他对主厨处处恭顺，动一下锅都要先等主厨点头。
那年七月，厨房热得让人受不了，炉子修好前已经有两名帮厨中暑晕倒。
卫生检查员认定冷藏间的电线状况不能再任其存在，勒令厨房停业整改。
那道看起来最朴素的品鉴菜其实最会骗人：明明只有三样食材，尝起来却像十样。
那年春天被辞退的一个厨子从此心怀报复，开始用假名到处打一星差评。
尽管如此，老板还是不屈不挠，一连一个月，每条评论都亲自回复。
与房东的纠纷越闹越僵，直到双方最终在法庭上达成和解。

passages.title: 葡萄园世仇
en: My grandmother said our feud was, {{for-what-its-worth|for what it's worth}}, older than anyone alive could explain.
The vineyard dispute wasn't unusual {{per-se}}; farms nearby often split over a fence line.
Ours was different: the quarrel {{cast-a-long-shadow|cast a long shadow}} over three generations who barely knew why.
Old stories should be taken {{with-a-pinch-of-salt|with a pinch of salt}}: each side blamed the other's grandfather.
Most agree the whole thing seems to {{stem-from|stem from}} a single missed harvest payment in 1948.
A reconciliation dinner was arranged twice; both times it {{fall-through|fell through}}.
Visits between the branches stayed {{intermittent}} at best: a card some years, nothing in others.
{{conversely}}, the two sides' lawyers spoke constantly, filing paperwork over a well nobody used.
Every mediation between the cousins grew {{acrimonious}} within minutes, old grievances dragged out again.
My aunt alone stayed {{tenacious}}, driving three hours each spring for talks nobody believed would work.
zh: 祖母总说，这场家族恩怨说句实话，连她这个年纪的人都说不清究竟是怎么开始的。
这场葡萄园纠纷本身并不稀奇，附近不少农庄都为一道篱笆界线闹掰过。
我们家不同的是，最初那场争执一路投下阴影，笼罩了三代人，可谁都记不清起因了。
家里流传的说法该打个折扣地听：双方都把责任推到对方的祖父头上。
大多数人都认为，整件事的根源是1948年一次漏付的收成款。
和解晚宴筹备过两次，两次都黄了。
两支家族之间的往来时断时续：好的年份寄张贺卡，差的年份干脆音信全无。
反过来，两边的律师倒是联系不断，为一口早没人用的井打了好多年官司文书。
表亲之间每次调解，没几分钟就吵得不可开交，陈年旧怨又被翻出来一遍。
只有姑姑始终锲而不舍，每年春天都要开三小时车去再谈一轮，尽管谁都不信能谈成。

passages.title: 流亡史学家讲座
en: To call the regime harsh would be a serious {{understatement}}, the visiting historian told her class.
{{first-and-foremost|First and foremost}}, she said, fear had run the country for thirty years, not one leader.
It had started as a plain {{dictatorship}}: one general cancelling elections and naming himself president.
What followed was outright {{tyranny}}: neighbors informing on neighbors, whole villages punished for one missing report.
A student asked, almost {{offhandedly}}, whether things had really been that bad.
That question seemed to {{unsettle}} her more than any other, and she paused before answering.
She'd learned to listen {{attentively}} even to careless questions; that was how the regime once caught people.
On the general's health, the ministry was never {{forthcoming}}, releasing nothing in his last two years.
The debate that followed grew {{acrimonious}}, students accusing each other of excusing or exaggerating the past.
Still, the historian stayed {{tenacious}}, answering every last question long after the bell had rung.
zh: 把那个政权说成严酷，都算是轻描淡写了，来访的史学家一开口就这样告诉全班。
她说，首先要弄清楚的是，让这个国家提心吊胆了三十年的是恐惧本身，而不是哪一个领导人。
这个政权起初不过是个简单的独裁：一名将军取消选举，自封总统。
接下来的就是彻头彻尾的暴政：邻里互相告发，一份漏交的报告能牵连整座村子。
一名学生随口问了一句，语气漫不经心，仿佛这事到底有多糟根本无关紧要。
这个问题反倒让她比别的问题更不能平静，她顿了好一会儿才开口回答。
她说自己学会了连再随意的问题也要专注地听，因为当年那个政权正是靠这个抓人的。
至于那位将军的健康状况，当局始终讳莫如深，他统治的最后两年没有透露过一点真实消息。
随后的讨论变得火药味十足，学生们互相指责对方要么在为往事开脱，要么在夸大其词。
尽管如此，这位史学家还是锲而不舍，铃声响了很久之后仍在回答最后几个问题。

passages.title: 面包店的姐弟之争
en: When their father died, Elena and Dov inherited the family bakery, but peace did not last.
Elena was {{personable}} enough to calm down even the most impatient regulars at the counter.
Dov, by contrast, was {{obdurate}} about the recipes, refusing to change a single ingredient.
He had been {{headstrong}} since childhood, storming off rather than admitting he was wrong.
One morning a customer shouted that the bread was stale, {{obnoxious}} and loud enough for the street to hear.
Their aunt, who kept the books, resorted to {{reproof}} when the argument spiraled out of control.
He turned {{pugnacious}} whenever his judgment was questioned, squaring up to customers like rivals.
Worse, the landlord next door proved {{implacable}}, raising the rent however hard the siblings pleaded.
Elena discovered Dov had signed a new flour contract behind her back — the move was {{underhand}}, and their aunt called it {{contemptible}}.
Only an old photo of their father baking before dawn was enough to {{assuage}} the anger between them.
zh: 父亲去世后，埃琳娜姐弟俩接手了家里的面包店，可太平日子没能维持多久。
柜台前，埃琳娜为人随和讨喜，再没耐心的老顾客，几句话就能被她哄消气。
多夫却是个死脑筋，对配方寸步不让，父亲传下来的方子，哪怕一样料都不肯换。
他从小就犟，认死理，宁可摔门走人也不肯认错。
一天早上，一个顾客扯着嗓子嚷嚷面包不新鲜，讨人嫌又吵，半条街都听得见。
姑姑管着店里的账，见争吵闹得没完没了，索性狠狠训了他一顿。
只要有人质疑他的判断，他就摆出要打架的架势，见谁都跟仇人似的。
更糟的是，隔壁房东铁石心肠，任凭姐弟俩怎么求情，租金说涨就涨。
埃琳娜后来发现，多夫瞒着她偷偷签了一份新的面粉供货合同——这一手偷偷摸摸，姑姑更是直接说他下作。
最后，还是一张父亲天不亮就揉面的旧照片，多少抚平了两人之间的怒气。

passages.title: 青铜船首像修复记
en: The museum's lab had run {{deficit|deficits}} for three years, and trustees were losing patience.
The salvaged bronze figurehead was so brittle that {{circumspection}} was the rule whenever it was handled.
Wedged into a concrete cradle, it sat completely {{immobile}}, far too heavy to shift.
The lead conservator, {{tenacious}} after three failed funding pitches, refused to sell it for scrap.
One Tuesday a technician cleaning its cloak found a faint inscription and shouted, {{ecstatic}}, loud enough to bring the whole lab running.
The lettering confirmed what everyone feared: decades of salt-water {{degradation}} had eaten into the metal.
To halt it, she ordered a coating of alloy that stayed {{unreactive}} to salt-laden air.
A newly hired assistant, {{impetuous}} as ever, wanted to scrub the whole figurehead with solvent that same afternoon.
Word of the find reached a retired shipowner who was {{provident}} enough to have quietly saved for exactly this emergency.
His donation covered the repair, but the next board meeting still turned {{acrimonious}} over who deserved credit.
zh: 博物馆的修复室已经连续三年入不敷出，理事会的耐心快要耗尽了。
那尊打捞上来的青铜船首像太脆了，谁碰它都得格外小心。
它嵌在水泥底座里，纹丝不动，重得连修复室几个人都挪不动。
主修复师三次申请经费都碰了壁，却依然咬紧牙关，不肯把它当废铜卖掉。
一个周二，一名技师在清理它衣袍的褶皱时，发现了一行模糊的刻字，狂喜之下大喊一声，把整间实验室的人都引了过来。
刻字印证了大家一直担心的事：常年的海水侵蚀早已深深啃进了金属内部。
为了止住这个过程，她让人给表面镀了一层合金，泡在含盐的空气里也不起化学反应。
新来的助理一如既往地毛躁，当天下午就想拿溶剂把整尊像擦一遍。
消息传到一位早已退休、颇有远见的船东耳中——他多年前就悄悄存了一笔钱，专门应对这类意外。
他的捐款解决了修复费用，可下一次理事会上，大家还是为这份功劳该算谁的吵得不可开交。
